There are 60 minutes in an hour.

Regarding the competitor's strategy, Streamline Autos' direct-to-consumer (DTC) model for electric vehicles presents a significant market impact and several implications for our business. By bypassing traditional dealerships, they reduce overhead costs, allowing for more competitive pricing that could pressure our margins or force us to reconsider our own pricing structures. Furthermore, their direct engagement with customers provides them with first-party data on consumer behavior, preferences, and pain points. This data advantage enables them to iterate on their product and marketing strategies more rapidly than competitors relying on third-party dealership feedback.

For our business, this implies a need to evaluate our own distribution channels. If we rely heavily on traditional dealership networks, we may be at a disadvantage in terms of both cost efficiency and customer insight. We should consider whether to develop a hybrid sales model, enhance our direct digital engagement capabilities, or leverage our existing dealer relationships to offer superior service and value-added experiences that Streamline Autos cannot easily replicate. Additionally, we must monitor their pricing closely and be prepared to adjust our value proposition to retain market share in the evolving EV landscape.
